1. Parties and scope

These terms apply between Yasin Büyüktepe ("MESA") and everyone who uses mesamemory.dev or creates a MESA account. By creating an account you accept these terms.

2. The service

MESA is an open-source project in alpha. The website, documentation, benchmark reports and account services are offered free of charge and “as is”. Features may change or be withdrawn. MESA is not qualified for production use.

3. Your account

  • You must be 18 or over and give accurate information.
  • Keep your password secret; you are responsible for activity on your account.
  • Tell us at once if you think your account has been misused.
  • You can close your account at any time by applying as described in the KVKK notice.

4. Acceptable use

  • Do not attack, overload or try to bypass the security of the site or its services.
  • Do not create accounts automatically or on behalf of others without permission.
  • Do not use the services for unlawful purposes.

5. Benchmark data and software

Access to research data packages is granted case by case and is subject to the conditions shown at approval and the licence of each package. The MESA software is licensed separately under the Apache License 2.0; these terms do not change that licence.

6. Intellectual property

Texts, design and benchmark reports on the site belong to MESA unless stated otherwise. Short quotations with attribution are welcome.

7. Liability

To the extent permitted by law, MESA is not liable for indirect damage, data loss or interruptions arising from the use of the free services. Rights that cannot be limited by law, including consumer rights under Law No. 6502, remain reserved.

8. Suspension and termination

We may suspend or close accounts that break these terms. You can stop using the services at any time.

9. Changes

We may update these terms. Material changes are announced on the site and, for account holders, by email before they take effect.

10. Governing law

Turkish law applies. The courts and enforcement offices of Manisa have jurisdiction; in consumer matters, consumer arbitration committees and consumer courts remain competent.
